messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Project mentor / feedback
parts:
Hello List,

I have a project idea and was wondering if anyone would be willing
serve as a mentor. Also, I was hoping to get some feedback regarding
whether the community would be interested in funding it.

Deducer is a graphical user interface for R. It is light weight and
available across many platforms and consoles. Though it is difficult
for programmers to realize sometimes, but ease of use is a major
barrier in the use of R for competent people who otherwise have a
solid understanding of statistics (not to mention students).

The package has been pretty successful so far. While package
statistics are difficult to come by, the manual (http://
www.deducer.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php?n=Main.DeducerManual) has had
>25,000 page views since September by >6,000 unique visitors.

Though there are many areas of the package that can use work, I would
like to focus on its biggest current weakness. I propose to build an
interface to Hadley's ggplot2 package. Separate dialogs would be
created for many common types of graphs (histogram, box-plot, scatter
plot, etc.), as well as a general chart builder along the same lines
as Jeroen's web app (http://www.yeroon.net/ggplot2/).

Each dialog would be simple to use, and yet contain much (if not all)
of the functionality required by a serious data analyst. For example:
* Shape
* Size
* Color
* Paneling (grid and wrap)
* Regression lines (smooth, polynomial and linear)
* Labels / Title
* Transparency
* Preview
* etc

I'm fairly self sufficient at this point, so the mentor can be
involved as much or as little as he/she wishes. Would anyone be
willing to work with me on this? Is this something would be likely to
be funded?

Though the above is close to my heart, if it doesn't work out I would
also be interested in working on Hadley's cran statistics proposal. A
few students and I put together a prototype for the UCLA CRAN mirror
last quarter for a class project (http://neolab.stat.ucla.edu/
cranstats/). The data is not live now, but it should give some idea of
what I was thinking about.

I would propose:
*Make a general purpose package for the parsing of APACHE logs.
*Write some specialized code for extracting information from CRAN
server logs.
*Auto-generated html summary pages.
*Easy aggregation of statistics across mirrors.
*Integrate aggregated stats with crantastic.

The first project is more ambitious, and much more work. On the other
hand it is more focused on pleasing R users than R developers.

Any feedback is more than welcome...


Cheers,
Ian Fellows
